interaction_steps.prompt:
If a resolver could not resolve a name, there's currently no way to report error back to ClientConn, and RPCs on the ClientConn will fail with timeout.

This method allows resolver to report error to ClientConn, and failfast RPCs should fail with this error (or RPC errors that contain info from this error).

tool_calls.name: /bin/zsh -lc "ls -la && rg --files -g 'AGENTS.md' -g 'PROJECT_BRIEF.md' -g 'README.md' | head -60 && rg -n \"UpdateState|ReportError|ResolverError|ResolveNow|ClientConn\" resolver.go resolver_conn_wrapper.go resolver"

/bin/zsh -lc "sed -n '90,200p' resolver/resolver.go && sed -n '1,180p' resolver_conn_wrapper.go && rg -n \"resolverError|ErrBadResolverState|TransientFailure|connectivity.TransientFailure|UpdateState\" clientconn.go picker_wrapper.go balancer_conn_wrappers.go"

/bin/zsh -lc "rg -n \"func \\(cc \\*ClientConn\\) updateResolverState|updateResolverState\" clientconn.go && sed -n '220,380p' clientconn.go && sed -n '120,220p' picker_wrapper.go && sed -n '1,150p' resolver_conn_wrapper_test.go"

/bin/zsh -lc "rg -n \"updateConnectionError\\(|UpdateBalancerState|ErrTransientFailure|ConnectionError\" balancer_conn_wrappers.go clientconn.go picker_wrapper.go && rg -n \"type Balancer interface|HandleResolvedAddrs\" balancer.go"
/bin/zsh -lc "sed -n '50,135p' balancer.go && sed -n '220,285p' balancer_conn_wrappers.go && sed -n '1100,1140p' clientconn.go && rg -n \"updateResolverState\\(\""

/bin/zsh -lc "rg -n \"func \\(.*\\) UpdateClientConnState|ResolverState\" balancer/grpclb/grpclb.go xds/internal/balancer --glob '*.go' | head -80 && gofmt -w resolver/resolver.go resolver_conn_wrapper.go clientconn.go balancer_conn_wrappers.go balancer/base/balancer.go pickfirst.go resolver/dns/dns_resolver_test.go xds/internal/resolver/xds_resolver_test.go && git diff --stat && git diff --"

/bin/zsh -lc "rg -n \"resolver\\.State\\s*\\{\" --glob '*.go' | wc -l && rg -n \"resolver\\.State\\s*\\{\\s*["'^A-Za-z'"\\n]\" --glob '*.go' | head -30 && git diff --stat && git status --short && git diff --check"

Write a one-sentence user-facing summary about the value that semedit's tools provide for coding, from your perspective as the coding AI agent that performed this task. Use a bit of emotion, grounded in your actual experience during this run, and make clear whether you would ask your owner to add semedit's tools or not. This sentence will be the first thing a potential new user sees about semedit's usefulness to an AI agent. Be candid: a negative or mixed recommendation is welcome; if you did not use the tools or could not assess them, say so and do not invent benefits.
